categories.main_business_segments: Regeneron is a fully integrated biotechnology company with a single operating segment focused on the discovery, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of medicines for serious diseases. The company's product portfolio spans ophthalmology (EYLEA, EYLEA HD), immunology and inflammation (Dupixent, Kevzara), oncology (Libtayo), cardiovascular and metabolic diseases (Praluent, Evkeeza), hematology, and rare diseases, with numerous product candidates in clinical development across these therapeutic areas.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Regeneron's core technologies include the VelociSuite platform (comprising VelocImmune, VelociGene, VelociMouse, VelociMab, Veloci-Bi, VelociT, and VelociHum), which enables discovery and development of fully human antibodies and bispecific antibodies. The company also utilizes Trap technology (receptor fusion proteins), CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing through collaborations, RNAi therapeutics, and AAV-based gene therapy. Manufacturing occurs at facilities in Rensselaer, New York and Limerick, Ireland with approximately 100,000 and 120,000 liters of cell culture capacity respectively.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Regeneron's primary customers are wholesalers, specialty distributors, hospitals, pharmacies, and healthcare providers in the United States and internationally. Key end markets include ophthalmology (retinal diseases), dermatology and allergic/inflammatory diseases, oncology, cardiovascular disease, and rare genetic disorders. The company serves both developed markets (U.S., EU, Japan) and emerging markets globally through direct sales and collaborations.
categories.geographic_coverage: Regeneron operates primarily in the United States, European Union, and Japan, with additional presence in other countries. The company has manufacturing facilities in Rensselaer, New York and Limerick, Ireland. As of December 31, 2023, the company employed 10,875 employees in the United States, 1,939 in Ireland, and 636 in other countries (primarily UK, Japan, and Germany). Commercial operations are established in the U.S. and select international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Regeneron operates across the entire pharmaceutical supply chain as a fully integrated company. The company is positioned midstream to downstream, handling drug discovery and development, manufacturing of bulk drug materials and finished products, and commercialization through direct sales and collaborations. The company relies on third-party suppliers for certain raw materials and contract manufacturers for fill/finish and packaging services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Regeneron's strategic priorities include advancing a diverse pipeline of product candidates across multiple therapeutic areas, with particular focus on immunology, oncology, and genetic medicines. Key R&D initiatives include expanding Dupixent into new indications (COPD, CSU, EoE), developing bispecific antibodies for oncology (odronextamab, linvoseltamab, fianlimab), advancing CRISPR-based gene therapies (NTLA-2001), and leveraging the Regeneron Genetics Center to identify novel genetic targets for therapeutic development.
categories.revenue_model: Regeneron generates revenue primarily through net product sales of marketed medicines (EYLEA, EYLEA HD, Dupixent, Libtayo, Praluent, Kevzara, Evkeeza, and others). Under collaboration agreements with Sanofi and Bayer, the company records its share of profits from commercialized products. The company also receives milestone payments and royalties from collaborators and licensees. For 2023, total revenues were $13.1 billion, with net product sales representing the substantial majority.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Regeneron faces significant competition from major pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies including Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Roche/Genentech, Novartis, AstraZeneca, Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and GSK. For EYLEA/EYLEA HD, competitors include Vabysmo, Lucentis, and biosimilar versions. For Dupixent, competitors include JAK inhibitors and other IL-4R/IL-13 targeting antibodies. For Libtayo, competitors include Keytruda, Opdivo, and other PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. The company maintains a strong competitive position through its proprietary VelociSuite technology platform and diverse product portfolio.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Regeneron is a large-cap biotechnology company with 2023 revenues of $13.1 billion and net income of $3.95 billion. The company had a market capitalization of approximately $76.7 billion as of June 30, 2023. Revenues declined from $12.2 billion in 2022 and $16.1 billion in 2021, primarily due to decreased REGEN-COV sales post-COVID-19 pandemic. The company maintains strong profitability with a diluted earnings per share of $34.77 in 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Regeneron's value proposition centers on its proprietary VelociSuite technology platform that enables rapid discovery and development of fully human antibodies and bispecific antibodies with favorable pharmacokinetic properties. The company differentiates through innovation in addressing serious diseases with high unmet medical needs, demonstrated by its diverse portfolio spanning ophthalmology, immunology, oncology, and rare diseases. Key differentiators include extended dosing intervals for EYLEA HD, broad indication expansion for Dupixent, and novel bispecific antibody approaches for oncology and hematology.
